title: 2014 AMC 10A Problem 24
statement: A sequence of natural numbers is constructed by listing the first \(4,\) then skipping one, listing the next \(5,\) skipping \(2,\) listing \(6,\) skipping \(3,\) and on the \(n\)th iteration, listing \(n+3\) and skipping \(n.\) The sequence begins \[1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,10,13.\] What is the \(500{,}000\)th number in the sequence?

solutions.text:
After \(n\) full iterations, the number of listed terms is \(4+5+\cdots+(n+3)=\frac{n(n+7)}2\).

We need the largest \(n\) with \(\frac{n(n+7)}2<500000\). Since \(996\cdot1003=998988\), after \(996\) iterations there are \(499494\) listed numbers.

The first number listed in iteration \(997\) is one more than the total of all listed and skipped numbers so far, namely \(996^2+4\cdot996+1=996001\).

The \(500000\)th listed number is the \(500000-499494=506\)th number of this next block, so it is \(996001+505=996506\).

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Count how many terms have been listed after \(n\) full iterations
Then locate the desired term inside the next listed block
